chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But over those who take him as their guardian.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/master

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's authority (hukm) is not absolute over all believers but is conditional upon their voluntary submission, distinguishing between those who follow his whispers and those who remain steadfast in faith. This narration underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (ikhtiyar), affirming that while Satan has power over the heedless, he receives, he cannot compel the faithful to sin without their consent. The Imam’s explanation serves to comfort believers by delineating the scope of satanic influence, reinforcing that spiritual victory depends on conscious adherence to divine guidance rather than inevitable predation by Shaytan.
